title: Ascending chain condition for quasi-coherent submodules on a Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] with quasi-compact underlying space) and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Every increasing sequence $\mathcal F_1\subseteq\mathcal F_2\subseteq\dots\subseteq\mathcal F$ of quasi-coherent submodules is eventually constant. In particular every nonempty set of quasi-coherent submodules of $\mathcal F$, and every nonempty set of quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals of $\mathcal O_X$, has a maximal element for inclusion.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y8 (lemma-acc-coherent); the maximal-element form is how the proofs of Proposition 088C and Theorem 088E use it

proof.text: *Step 1 (a finite affine cover with Noetherian rings).* By [pqf-def-locnoeth] $X$ has an affine open covering by opens $U$ with $\mathcal O_X(U)$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; since $X$ is quasi-compact, finitely many of them, $U_1,\dots,U_r$, cover $X$. Put $A_i=\mathcal O_X(U_i)$, a Noetherian ring, and recall that $U_i$ is an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] (isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ inducing the identity on global sections). ('Choose a finite affine open covering.')

*Step 2 ($\mathcal F(U_i)$ is a finite $A_i$-module).* $\mathcal F$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent], so it is of finite type, and it is of finite presentation: every point has an open $W$ with a surjection $\pi:\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_W$, whose kernel is of finite type by coherence, so after shrinking to an open $V\ni x$ there is a surjection $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to\operatorname{Ker}(\pi)|_V$, and $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_V\to0$ is exact. Hence $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](0), and, being quasi-coherent of finite type, $\mathcal F(U_i)$ is a finitely generated $A_i$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] for every $i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](c). For $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ (the case of ideal sheaves) no coherence is needed: $\mathcal O_X(U_i)=A_i$ is generated by $1$. For a quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F$ (a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module, $\mathcal G(U)\subseteq\mathcal F(U)$ an $\mathcal O_X(U)$-submodule for every open $U$, which is quasi-coherent), $\mathcal G(U_i)$ is an $A_i$-submodule of $\mathcal F(U_i)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y8 (lemma-acc-coherent), proof (finiteness of the sections on an affine open is Properties, Lemma 01PB, carried by lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine)

proof.text: *Step 3 (a quasi-coherent submodule is determined by its sections on the cover).* Let $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal G'\subseteq\mathcal F$ be quasi-coherent submodules with $\mathcal G(U_i)=\mathcal G'(U_i)$ for $i=1,\dots,r$. Then $\mathcal G=\mathcal G'$. Indeed, fix $i$ and let $\iota:\mathcal G|_{U_i}\to\mathcal G'|_{U_i}$ be the inclusion. Transport to $\operatorname{Spec}A_i\cong U_i$ (Step 1): the restrictions $\mathcal G|_{U_i}$, $\mathcal G'|_{U_i}$ are quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2), with global sections $\mathcal G(U_i)$, $\mathcal G'(U_i)$. The counits $\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}:\widetilde{\mathcal G(U_i)}\to\mathcal G|_{U_i}$ and $\varepsilon_{\mathcal G'}$ are isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3), and by naturality (1) $\iota\circ\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}=\varepsilon_{\mathcal G'}\circ\widetilde{\iota_{U_i}}$; here $\iota_{U_i}$ is the identity of $\mathcal G(U_i)=\mathcal G'(U_i)$, so $\widetilde{\iota_{U_i}}$ and hence $\iota$ are isomorphisms, i.e. $\mathcal G(V)=\mathcal G'(V)$ for every open $V\subseteq U_i$. Now let $V\subseteq X$ be any open and $s\in\mathcal G'(V)$. For each $i$, $s|_{V\cap U_i}\in\mathcal G'(V\cap U_i)=\mathcal G(V\cap U_i)$; these sections of the sheaf $\mathcal G$ agree on overlaps (they are restrictions of $s$ in $\mathcal F$), so they glue to $t\in\mathcal G(V)$, and $t=s$ in $\mathcal F(V)$ since $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf and both restrict to $s|_{V\cap U_i}$. So $\mathcal G'(V)=\mathcal G(V)$. (The same argument as Step 2(i) of lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y8 (lemma-acc-coherent), proof ('Hence the lemma follows': the passage from the cover to $X$, written out)

proof.text: *Step 4 (ascending chain condition).* Let $\mathcal F_1\subseteq\mathcal F_2\subseteq\dots\subseteq\mathcal F$ be quasi-coherent submodules. For each $i$, $(\mathcal F_n(U_i))_n$ is an increasing sequence of $A_i$-submodules of the finitely generated $A_i$-module $\mathcal F(U_i)$ over the Noetherian ring $A_i$ (Steps 1, 2), so by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-module-acc](1) (Algebra, Lemma 00IK) there is $n_i$ with $\mathcal F_m(U_i)=\mathcal F_{n_i}(U_i)$ for $m\ge n_i$. Let $n=\max_i n_i$ (finitely many $i$). For $m\ge n$ we have $\mathcal F_n\subseteq\mathcal F_m$ and $\mathcal F_n(U_i)=\mathcal F_m(U_i)$ for all $i$, so $\mathcal F_n=\mathcal F_m$ by Step 3.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y8 (lemma-acc-coherent), proof ('On each member of the covering we get stabilization by Algebra, Lemma 00IK')

proof.text: *Step 5 (maximal elements).* Let $\Phi$ be a nonempty set of quasi-coherent submodules of $\mathcal F$ (for ideal sheaves take $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, for which Step 2 gives $\mathcal O_X(U_i)=A_i$ finitely generated without coherence). Define nonempty subsets $\Phi=\Phi^{(0)}\supseteq\Phi^{(1)}\supseteq\dots\supseteq\Phi^{(r)}$ inductively: given $\Phi^{(i-1)}\neq\emptyset$, the set $\{\mathcal G(U_i):\mathcal G\in\Phi^{(i-1)}\}$ of $A_i$-submodules of $\mathcal F(U_i)$ is nonempty, so it has a maximal element $M_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-module-acc](2); put $\Phi^{(i)}=\{\mathcal G\in\Phi^{(i-1)}:\mathcal G(U_i)=M_i\}\neq\emptyset$. Pick $\mathcal G\in\Phi^{(r)}$. If $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal G'\in\Phi$, then by induction on $i$, $\mathcal G'\in\Phi^{(i)}$: if $\mathcal G'\in\Phi^{(i-1)}$ then $\mathcal G'(U_i)\supseteq\mathcal G(U_i)=M_i$ and maximality of $M_i$ give $\mathcal G'(U_i)=M_i$. So $\mathcal G'(U_i)=\mathcal G(U_i)$ for all $i$, and $\mathcal G'=\mathcal G$ by Step 3. Hence $\mathcal G$ is maximal in $\Phi$. (This is the form in which the proofs of Cohomology of Schemes, Proposition 088C and Theorem 088E use Lemma 01Y8; written by the agent, since the source states only the chain form.)
